headline: Attendance is the main concern: 69 students are chronically absent, it rose since Q1, and it overlaps with academics more than any other pair.

keyNumbers.label: moved up a tier since Q1

bigPicture.label: chronically absent, up from 21% in Q1
bigPicture.point: Attendance flags more students than academics or behavior, and it is the only area that grew.
bigPicture.read: Most students flagged for academics are also flagged for attendance, so missed days may be driving many academic flags.
bigPicture.do: Treat attendance as the first lever for this snapshot, before adding academic interventions.
bigPicture.doLess: Separate academic and attendance plans for the same students.

bigPicture.label: students moved up a tier since Q1
bigPicture.point: More students moved up a tier than down, so needs are growing faster than they are being met.
bigPicture.read: Did the students who moved up already have a tier 2 support, or were they new to the list?
bigPicture.do: At the next MTSS meeting, review whether current tier 2 supports have exit criteria.

counselor.label: of grade 9 flagged for attendance
counselor.point: Grade 9 has the highest attendance rate of any grade, above the school's 23%.
counselor.read: Are these absences full days or missed first periods? The attendance office can pull period-level data.
counselor.do: Start a 6-week check-in group for grade 9 students with attendance flags.
counselor.doLess: One-time attendance letters with no follow-up.

counselor.label: flagged in attendance and academics
counselor.point: This is the largest overlap between two areas.
counselor.do: Use one shared plan for these students that covers both attendance and course recovery.

administrator.label: chronically absent, up from 21%
administrator.point: The rise came while every other area held steady or was not compared.
administrator.read: Did anything change in Q2 schedules or start times that could affect morning arrival?
administrator.do: Ask the attendance office for a monthly report by grade and period through Q4.

administrator.label: students in Tier 3
administrator.point: Tier 3 holds 10% of students, which strains small-group and individual support time.
administrator.do: Protect one weekly block for the intervention team to review Tier 3 cases.

teachers.label: chronically absent, up from 21% in Q1
teachers.point: More than a fifth of students missed 10% or more of days.
teachers.read: Are absences clustered in first period or on Mondays? The attendance office can check.
teachers.do: In grade 9, greet and log first-period arrivals for 4 weeks.
teachers.doLess: Whole-class attendance reminders, which reach students already there.

teachers.label: flagged for academics, up from 12%
teachers.read: With most academic flags also absent often, missing work may be the gap more than skill.
teachers.do: Offer a make-up window for missed assignments before grades post.
teachers.doLess: Zeroes for missing work from absent days.

supportTeam.label: newly flagged for attendance since Q1
supportTeam.point: New attendance flags outnumber the ones that cleared.
supportTeam.do: Contact families of newly flagged students within 2 weeks of the flag.

supportTeam.label: flagged for behavior
supportTeam.point: Behavior flags only 7% of students and was not in the Q1 files.
supportTeam.read: Are behavior incidents logged the same way in every grade?
supportTeam.do: Check referral logging practices with each grade team before Q3.

connections.label: flagged in attendance and academics
connections.point: These students need one plan, not three.

steps.step: Share the list of missing assignments for these students each Friday.
Meet with each student weekly to set an attendance and work goal.
Reach families of students who miss two goals in a row.

connections.label: students in Tier 3
connections.point: Tier 3 support depends on protected time and clear handoffs.

steps.step: Schedule a weekly intervention team block.
Bring a short status for each Tier 3 case to that block.

goals.statement: By [date], all students will decrease the chronic absence rate from 23% to [target set by counselor].
By [date], all students will decrease the number in Tier 3 from 31 to [target set by counselor].

limits: Counts under 10 are not shown and are unknown. Behavior was not in the Q1 files, so it was not compared. Change counts only the 295 students in both snapshots.
